text: UK unemployment rate fell to 3.8% in the three months to January 2024, down from 4.2% a year earlier, according to the Office for National Statistics.
The employment rate in the UK was 74.5% in December 2023, the highest since comparable records began.
US nonfarm payrolls increased by 353,000 in January 2024, with the unemployment rate unchanged at 3.7%.
Average hourly earnings for all employees rose 4.5% year-over-year in January 2024, outpacing inflation for the first time in two years.
Global GDP growth slowed to 2.4% in 2023, with advanced economies growing at just 1.5%, according to World Bank projections.
OECD composite leading indicators point to a gradual recovery in GDP growth across member countries in the second half of 2024.
US federal debt held by the public reached 97% of GDP at end of fiscal year 2023, the highest since World War II, per CBO projections.
UK CPI inflation fell to 2.3% in April 2024, down from a peak of 11.1% in October 2022.
US CPI rose 3.5% year-over-year in March 2024, slightly above the Federal Reserve's 2% target.
OECD average inflation was 5.4% in 2023, down from 9.4% in 2022, driven by falling energy prices.
NHS England waiting lists reached a record 7.6 million in September 2023, with 3.3 million waiting more than 18 weeks.
Global infant mortality has declined by 59% since 1990, falling to 27 deaths per 1,000 live births in 2021.
Child poverty in the UK is projected to rise to 24% in 2023-24, up from 19% before the 2022 cost-of-living crisis, according to IFS.
The UK government built approximately 234,000 new homes in 2022-23, below the 300,000 annual target.
Police recorded crime in England and Wales fell 6% in the year to June 2023, to 6.7 million offences.
Global CO2 emissions from fossil fuels reached a record 36.8 billion tonnes in 2023, up 1.1% from 2022.
UK carbon emissions fell 5.4% in 2023, the lowest since the 1800s, driven by reduced coal use.
OECD countries spent an average of $12,000 per primary student annually in 2020, with the UK spending $11,200.
NATO defence spending targets require members to spend at least 2% of GDP. The UK spent 2.07% of GDP on defence in 2023.
Global merchandise trade fell 5% in value in 2023 due to lower commodity prices, though volumes grew modestly.
Food bank use in the UK rose sharply in 2022-23, with the Trussell Trust reporting record 3 million emergency food parcels.
UK real wages fell 2.2% in 2022-23 when adjusted for inflation, the largest annual fall since records began in 2001.
